steps.name: Frightened Student
steps.text: Wh-What the hell is that?

steps.name: Frightened Student
steps.text: The Witch King's Spire...? Is that the Witch King's Spire?!

steps.name: Frightened Student
steps.text: The Witch King is back. That terrifying tyrant... that evil caster... He's back!

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Stop, don't turn back. Don't push—

steps.name: Enraged Student
steps.text: Hahaha, where would you even run? This is the punishment that the great Herkunftshorn is laying down on us. Burn! Burn!

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: What are you doing? You're attracting the flames!

steps.name: Enraged Student
steps.text: It's all over anyway. Why even bother lying to ourselves anymore, pretending to have dignity?

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Put out the fire! Put it out!

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: In formation—

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: No, it's coming this way, the entire school is— There's no stopping it!
The black flames engulf everything in their wake. Laughter, sobbing. Nothing is spared.
As the sound of thunder rips through the air, the thick layers of clouds above descend lower and lower, almost becoming one with the strange spire before them.
Some of the older students remember the history books that they happen to have read, deep inside the spire. The ones that went unburned.
They said that during the Battle of the Four Emperors, Herkunftshorn brought an Originium storm that ripped apart the skies above the battlefield, swallowing an entire Gaulish landship fleet at once.
And now, at that very same location, there remains a terrifying rift deep in the Catastrophe clouds, the screams of the sleepless dead reverberating within.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Herr Gesatzswächter, the curtain isn't going to hold.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: The students are all trying to escape. We can't stop them. Everyone has seen the spire. Sooner or later, the news will spread. Should we...

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Nein.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Lower the curtain. Concentrate all your energy on dealing with the black flames.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: It's not working!

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: This assault was more than enough to decimate a vanguard of Kazimierzian campaign knights.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Herkunftshorn's enchantments are not so easily removed.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: As the legend goes, the way he used Arts was fundamentally different from other casters. During the Battle of the Witch King's Spire years ago, only the Kaiserinnen were able to perform their melodies unimpeded. All other casters' Arts failed.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: ...That spire.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: We must lay siege to it, and take care of the problem at its source.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Brandt.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Do you hear that? The lightning has stopped.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: She's here! We're saved!

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Everyone, defend.
The clouds begin to crack.
There is no sound, no shaking, and no omen of any kind. A bolt of purple-black lightning simply crashes down from high above.
Likewise, it is not accompanied by any kind of flashy explosion or shocking roar.
It merely pierces the spire's body and crushes the seemingly impenetrable tower, layer after layer, from top to bottom.
By the time the first piece of falling rubble reaches the ground, the reborn 'Witch King's Spire' has already ceased to be, as though it had never existed in the first place.
Finally, the earth starts trembling, as though reacting to the spire's fall.

Behind the wall of Arts conjured by the Imperial casters, the crowd stands in terror with their eyes wide open. At the highest point of the ruins, they see a figure holding a sword emitting purple-black sparks of lightning.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Herkunftshorn's shadow will no longer be permitted to shroud Leithanian soil.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Especially not that of a fake.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: We're certainly dealing with a fake, but... it's really quite remarkable how easily his expectations were shattered.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: A shame she's just like her blond twin. Their souls were molded by Arts enchantments, and I'm afraid there are few ripples that I can perform with.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It's over.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: What your plans were for the Gesatzswächter is now irrelevant. You have failed.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Is that so?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Federico, you are as impatient as ever. The climax of a piece is never its end.
Arturia spreads her arms and falls backward into the air behind the railing.
Then, the remains of a sculpture lift her up, and she quickly rises even higher.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I'll be waiting for you at the end of the stairs.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What... just happened? The chamber rose... and then...

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: I grabbed you and jumped.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: That's right. You jumped without hesitation, without even checking on your poor old grandfather.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: There's no way anything would happen to you.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: You heartless little runt.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Grimmacht really didn't hold back with her sword. If I hadn't pulled you two out in time, you'd have been buried in the dirt alongside all those masked men.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What about Gerhard...?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Is he dead?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: He ran.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: But he won't get far. His body can't withstand Herkunftshorn's Arts. He will collapse in no time, like an Infected with rapidly deteriorating symptoms.

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: Huff... hah...

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: *cough*... Haha... so my body... really cannot become the Genesis Horn's vessel.

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: This sound...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Hello, Herr Scholar.

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: You were... waiting for me?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Correct. I visited this school just for you.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: If you don't mind me asking... Would you be willing to allow my melody to accompany you, as you reach the end of your life?

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: Danke. To a Leithanian, there is nothing more romantic than... dying to the sound of beautiful music.

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: My only regret is that Grimmacht came too soon, and I didn't get to meet Herkunftshorn.

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: He didn't awaken, and there was no one to answer my question. If he was truly so great, then why... why was he killed by mere men like us? And why must I carry the burden of that decision?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: In the end, you remain tormented by regret.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But Herr Scholar, you have never truly been free. Why must you feel regret over past decisions?

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: I'm... not free?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Your tattered, weary heart is now laid bare before me.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I can feel everything you feel. On the night of the battle at the Spire, your heart was filled with spite toward the tyrant. But aside from that... there was also doubt.

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: Of course. The man I was about to kill, Herkunftshorn, was the rightful ruler of Leithanien.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Then, what planted the seeds of that emotion?

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: You mean... what influenced me to think that?

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: Are you implying that someone was telling me to look up to Leithanien's king?

spans.text: Are you implying that someone was
to look up to Leithanien's king?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I've visited many places and collected a variety of music. I found that although each of them has a unique style, they all share some commonalities in their origin. And Leithanien's in particular is the most classical of them all.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: This country was born... from a Movement. A melody blending together ten tribes with different cultures. When language proves to be a barrier, music is the only means to communicate.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But why is that? Why would different wills produce similar experiences from the same melody?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Is there some kind of... power, binding both you and us?

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: Why do conflict and crisis always repeat in an endless spiral...? Why is it so hard to change Leithanien?

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: I know. Your music is telling me that I've always known. It's just that that power... it keeps me from finding it!

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: The answer is in my hands. My teacher never lied to me.

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: The golden melody... Leithanien's will... All of us Leithanians are trapped!

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: Haha... So it's true. I've never really had a choice.

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: It wasn't my fault.

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: It wasn't my fault!

steps.name: Gerhard
steps.text: Thank goodness.
The scholar realizes that he is once again standing at the highest point of Ludwigs-Universität.
This is the first time in twenty-three years that he's earnestly gazed at the sunset outside.
The clouds are fluffy, and although they're completely soaked in blood, they yet maintain their original shapes.
This is Leithanien's evening glow.

Gerhard Hoffmann notices that his body and the Güldenesgesatz have fallen together on the spiral staircase, while his consciousness drifts out the window with the melody and dissolves into the clouds.
He has never felt so free.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Stay quiet for a moment. I want to let his emotions... linger at my fingertips for a little longer.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I've heard that you call yourself an executioner. You've witnessed so many deaths, but have you ever truly touched the last bout of emotion that bursts forth at their final moments?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: An executor is more concerned with the deceased's last testament.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You make the living believe that their wills will be carried out even after death, while I allow their most splendid emotions to live on in music.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Both of us substantiate the meaning of having lived. We just go about it in different ways.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am here to execute my mission and nothing more. I have no need to listen to a sinner's sophistry.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: *sigh* We're family, and haven't seen each other for so long. Can't you at least hold a proper conversation, Federico? Who's to say I won't die tomorrow?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You intentionally put yourself in danger. It would not be entirely surprising if you did.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I wouldn't find it surprising either.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: We're all bound to die. When we do, our bodies give nutrients back to the land and become a part of new life. This is the meaning of our flesh. It's the circle of life.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But what about the meaning of our wills? When our consciousness fades, they will return to chaos.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: So what separates the living from the dead, one person from another, and us from the sunset and the breeze?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It's our emotions, Federico.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: If there is meaning to our lives outside of our bodies, if there truly is something that can resist the destined chaos...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Then it is only this very moment, all that I feel, and the melody transmuted from those feelings.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: That's why, as long as I still breathe, I can't stop playing.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am required to apprehend wanted criminals, but if necessary, I can also pull the trigger.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Oh, I don't doubt that.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It'll happen one day, and there's no doubt that it will be Federico Giallo who kills Arturia Giallo. But do you think that daylight can kill the dark night, order can kill chaos, and reason can kill emotion?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Layering metaphors cannot cover up the essential truth.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You are a criminal, and I am an executor. I pursue you in order to fulfill the contract that is my duty.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You believe uncertainty to be a kind of emotion. That's why you're always seeking answers through rational analysis. But it's not your rationality that's led you to me again and again. It's your confusion.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You saw and heard it yourself. Today, countless lives were lost in chaos.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: If only you'd followed my advice and given up on me, instead lending your aid to that envoy of the Empress... With your skills, and how sharp you are, you could've easily found the one hiding in the shadows, manipulating the chaos.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But again and again, you choose to prioritize looking for me.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You are where my duty lies. I will not regret my decision.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I know you won't.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But look. Now you've caught me.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: So... satisfy my curiosity, Federico. Do you feel no satisfaction, right this very moment?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Seize her.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: So you people came too.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Recover the Güldenesgesatz as well.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Arturia is my target.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Herr Federico Giallo, Executor of the Lateran Curia's Fifth Tribunal.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: It's extremely likely that the Sankta before you has committed what amounts to the highest offense in Leithanien. She must come with us for our investigation.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I thought the Gendarmerie was in charge of the upcoming inquest.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: It's the Kaiserin's orders to take Arturia.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Does that mean that you cannot guarantee Arturia will be dealt with according to the law?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: As I said, these are the Kaiserin's orders.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I have sent a total of twenty-seven explanatory letters, in addition to repeating my mission objective to the now-deceased officer-in-charge, Loris Bordin.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: In that case—

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Frau Jonas.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Would it be possible for Herr Executor to participate in Arturia's interrogation?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: That's not part of my orders. To Leithanien, Arturia is a most dangerous criminal. No one is to be allowed anywhere near her without Her Majesty's explicit permission.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Then I—

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: That includes you.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Let's go.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Will we meet again, Federico, before my consciousness fades away?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Jonas... They call her the cruelest executor in Grimmacht's Spire.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: How did she get here so fast? Did Grimmacht... I'll talk to her. I...

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Herr Executor... Don't you want to chase after them?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If Leithanien can ensure that Arturia will never commit a crime again, my highest priority mission objective will be considered complete.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: However, as she said, I feel no satisfaction in this.
It has become much quieter outside the spire, yet the black flames continue to burn.
Viviana has forgotten which floor of the spire she is on. The spiral stairs all look the same.
Her candlelight flickers a few times before finally going out.

steps.name: Gendarmerie C
steps.text: Frau... Droste?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Pym? Why are you still here?

steps.name: Gendarmerie C
steps.text: Ha... Haha... I'm in pretty bad shape. At least this way I won't be a bother to the kids.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You were burned by the black flames. Half your body is...

steps.name: Gendarmerie C
steps.text: It's fine.

steps.name: Gendarmerie C
steps.text: I'm glad I got to see you again. By seeing you, I can at least confirm that I haven't turned into some kind of monster that walks even in death.

steps.name: Gendarmerie C
steps.text: The disaster's been averted, right?

steps.name: Gendarmerie C
steps.text: The Empresses' Voice, the Gesatzswächter... they're all here, right? Are the Witch King's remains all dead, and the students safe?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I suppose so.

steps.name: Gendarmerie C
steps.text: Hm. It's strange. I saw the captain just now.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Herr Loris Bordin...?

steps.name: Gendarmerie C
steps.text: He said I did pretty well, and did the Gendarmerie proud. Once the ceremony's over, my mother will get the Kaiserin's black-gold medal.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But that's only for those who've fallen...

steps.name: Gendarmerie C
steps.text: It's hopeless for me, right?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I don't want to lie to you.

steps.name: Gendarmerie C
steps.text: Meine Dame, when I see you looking at me like that... It doesn't hurt so much anymore.

steps.name: Gendarmerie C
steps.text: Your candlelight... is so warm.

steps.name: Gendarmerie C
steps.text: When I first got to Zwillingstürme, I nearly gave up. I couldn't keep up with how exhausting the training was, day after day. Only when I saw that tiny light you held in the arena, lighting up every one of my... my...
He did not deserve to fall into eternal slumber on these spiral stairs.
If he could have just a little more light, a little more warmth.
Viviana knows that she is not a lighthouse, but she is capable of that much.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Auf Wiedersehen, Pym.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: May this candlelight accompany you as you drift into eternal slumber.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Grimmacht's envoy said she's just up ahead.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Step aside, Cora. Let me take care of the rubble here first.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Let me do it. You've already...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Wait. These footsteps...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Viviana!

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Frau Löwenstein... Herr Reiner...

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: ...Good.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Meine Herr?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Let him get some rest. Raising the curtain by force took its toll on his body.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But... he's still standing.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: He'd never let himself collapse in front of so many.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Brandt's really worn himself out, all these years.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Before the battle, he saw me as my father.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: That's always weighed heavily on his mind.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Twenty-three years ago, House Hochberg suffered great losses at the Witch King's Spire, and because of his position as a Gesatzswächter, Brandt wasn't able to come to their aid in time.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Because of that, Ernst, his closest friend and the heir to the Hochbergs, perished in battle... That's also why your father Werner had to succeed him as Kurfürst.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: The remorse he felt toward Ernst and Werner has been eating away at his soul all this time. And today, when forced to choose between destroying Sonata Spire and saving you, he chose you.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I never imagined...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I knew he'd make that choice.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I'd have done the same.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I was so scared back there... I'm prepared to make any sacrifice, if necessary. But you... Not you.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I'm glad we didn't lose you.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...I'm one of the lucky ones. On my way here, I came across many who've passed away.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I did my best, but I wasn't able to rescue everyone.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: The casters will figure out how to eliminate the black flames. The victims will be taken care of.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Things will get better.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: They won't have suffered for nothing. This place will be completely different tomorrow.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I'll make sure you get to see that for yourself, Viviana.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I promise.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: What a beautiful sunrise.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: (Humming)

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Barrier.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Mm... Mmm? Hm...

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: We know a thing or two about your Arts, Meine Dame.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Now, neither you nor your cello are capable of making a sound.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: (Silent humming)

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: You made up your mind.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The Voice of Mundane... I've been dying to have someone take it away. If you've no plans to use it as a bomb, then be my guest.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: So you finally believe me?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I... admit I owe you an apology. And a word of thanks. If it wasn't for you, then I might not be Ebenholz right now, but some other thing.

spans.text: I... admit I owe you an apology. And a word of thanks. If it wasn't for you, then I might not be Ebenholz right now, but some other

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But please, spare me all this nonsense about 'trust' or what have you. I'd rather not see you pounce on me and knock me out with your sword the moment I spit out the words 'I trust you.'

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: I wasn't planning to. For now.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...Well, that's nice.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Someone's playing the cello.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: They're mourning the victims with music.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It was just like this when I first met Gerhard.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: He told me that... through music, the wills of the dead are carried on through us.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: He was so quiet and gentle. I really thought he was...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'm an idiot, aren't I?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I couldn't even see through their masks. I couldn't even see... who was controlling my life.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: How I wish I could be more like... No matter how many obstacles he encountered, he never lost hope. He even smiled as he...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: This piece...

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: What's wrong?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Who's playing the cello up there?!

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: The dormitory isn't far. Maybe a student?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: That's impossible.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Calm down. We can't expose ourselves yet.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It's exactly the same... How could it be exactly the same?!

a.text: The Sky is blue and fine,
The Breeze lilts by in Song;

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Where did you learn to play like that?

steps.name: Motivated Student
steps.text: Huh? I'm nothing special, really.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Not your technique, you fool, your emotions! Where did you learn to play this cello piece almost exactly like he did?!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: No one else played like him. I checked over and over. After he died, I've been to so many places and listened to even more musicians play that same piece!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Who was your teacher?!

steps.name: Motivated Student
steps.text: Um... Arturia. My teacher's name is Arturia.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Is she a Sankta? A Sankta with very long hair, who dresses plainly?

steps.name: Motivated Student
steps.text: Do you know her too? I saw her just today. She told me to keep practicing here, without worrying about the sounds outside.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...Without worrying about the sounds?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: That Sankta... Is she a remnant of the Witch King too?!

steps.name: Motivated Student
steps.text: N-No, that's impossible. She's very kind.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Where is she? I need to see her. I need to question her myself! I...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Ugh!

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Another headache?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Did you know, Lessing? He and I... Everything in our lives was given to us by others. Our pain, our joy... our despair.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: So if even our hope...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Even our hope...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I don't know if I actually want that answer.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Have you thought it through?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Hohoh, what is there to think about? The school was burnt down by Herkunftshorn's embers. I could miss it all I want, but that wouldn't bring it back.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: I've forgotten... How long have I been in Leithanien? Five hundred years? Longer?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: When I first got here, there was nothing. No nomadic cities, no spires, no nobles. Hah, back then, everyone lived in the forests by the lakes. They lit fires to eat, and used rocks to shelter from the wind.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: To us, a few decades are more than though for a city to rise and fall, a man to go from young to old, or a pair of close companions to have a falling out and go their separate ways.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: That's right. It's been but an instant since this place went from Vedunien to Zwillingstürme. I wonder what the city will be called next.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: And when that lamb with the rotten luck and a brain full of nothing but melodies is taken care of, I'll fulfill my promise to you. After that, I think I'll take a stroll around town.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: And once that's done...

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: We'll leave.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Tell the nobles they can have a good night's sleep, for once.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: I've already explained it to them, long ago.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Explained what? That Liches aren't like Vampires and don't get involved with Military Commission business, so they can rest easy that this place won't be the next Londinium?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Do you really believe they simply don't understand, Grimmacht?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: And are you really so whimsically unaware of who stands behind those nobles that want to chase the Liches out?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: You two can deal with the fallout afterwards.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: The Liches have indeed stayed here for far too long. Knowledge should never have taken the side of any one nation or race.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Do you even know how many Leithanian terms our brats use in their writing these days? It's absolutely outrageous!

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: We should've left when Herkunftshorn bought the farm.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: This... is just a belated farewell.
The white-haired Lich lifts his hand.
As though having been granted permission, a large number of slender silhouettes appear beneath the setting sun.

Perhaps they'd been standing there the whole time. They were simply masquerading as ordinary students and faculty. However, from this moment onwards, they are no longer concerned with how different they are from other Leithanians.
The Liches all raise their hands.
Countless paper-thin strands of silk extend from their bodies and into the dark clouds up above.
Then, a radiance like starlight comes falling down. Looking up, many of the students see the sunset, the night, and the sunrise all at once.
Within that brimming radiance, the dark flames on the earth are extinguished without a sound. Not long after, the silk-threaded shadows also disappear into the dream-like rain.
Ever since, no more trace of the Liches could be found in Leithanien's spires.
